newsitem.title: USA: Okla. City prosecutors want to talk with FBI agent.
newsitem.headline: Okla. City prosecutors want to talk with FBI agent.

text.p: Prosecutors in the Oklahoma City bombing case said Tuesday they have no intention of intimidating an FBI agent they want to speak to without defence lawyers being present.

Dr. Frederic Whitehurst, an FBI crime investigator and self-described whistle blower, is believed to have information on operational problems at the FBI lab that could help the case of bombing suspect Timothy McVeigh.

Last week U.S. District Court Judge Richard Matsch granted defence attorneys a temporary restraining order preventing the prosecution from speaking privately with Whitehurst. McVeigh's attorneys fear the meeting would intimidate Whitehurst.
Prosecutors argued that if the defence attorneys believed after the interview that Whitehurst had been intimated, they could bring it up at the trial.

"Defense counsel's abilities in this regard will be enhanced by the fact that Whitehurst has created an extensive library of documents setting forth his allegations and suspicions, much of which has been shared with the defence in this case," prosecutors wrote.
The government attorneys also said that Whitehurst's "history demonstrates that he is not one to be intimated by an interview."
Prosecutors said Whitehurst has written 177 letters fo the Inspector General of the Department of Justice alleging misconduct and improper procedures at the FBI lab.

McVeigh and former army buddy Terry Nichols are charged with the April 19, 1995 bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah federal building in Oklahoma City which claimed the lives of 168 people and injured hundreds.
A date has not yet been set for the trial to be held in Denver but it is expected to be late this year or early in 1997.
